solutions.check: 30 entries, 60 crossings, 0 conflicts; answers matched to the grid by number, direction and length

clue.text: Driving and reversing a lot in branch of police

indicators.note: reversing tells us the whole assembled string is read from right to left
in places the 'a lot' word inside the police branch abbreviation

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police
a lot means many

explanation.surface: Someone driving and reversing a great deal while working in a police department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driving and reversing' reads as a motoring scene, but only 'Driving' is the definition; 'reversing' turns the whole assembled string round to give CIMANYD backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Driving as an adjective means energetic and forceful, a sense shared with this word.

clue.text: Possibly 4 succeeded in headquarters

definitions.note: 4 is a Russian emperor, one example of an autocrat

indicators.note: in places the single letter inside the word for headquarters

parts.note: a depot is a base or headquarters, especially military
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: Perhaps a Russian ruler came to power at a base.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian emperor ruled absolutely, so he is an example of a tyrant.

clue.text: Feed old city, one with grub found outside

indicators.note: found outside means the food word sits round the other pieces

parts.note: nosh is slang for food or grub
Ur is an ancient Sumerian city
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Feeding an ancient city, a lone figure finds food around.
explanation.definitionFit: To nourish is to give nourishment or sustenance, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Parcels containing a potter's support for plant

indicators.note: containing means the word for parcels holds the other pieces

parts.note: mail means parcels and letters
a rest supports the cue of a snooker player, who pots balls

explanation.surface: Packages holding a ceramicist's stand for a houseplant.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'potter' here pots snooker balls, and the rest is the cue support.
explanation.definitionFit: Mare's tail is an aquatic plant with whorled leaves, also a name for horsetail.

clue.text: Vehicle carrying unknown person of great power

indicators.note: carrying means the vehicle word holds the extra letter

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
Z is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A car transports a mysterious powerful figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Applied loosely, the Russian emperor's title is used for any powerful official or overlord.

clue.text: An innocent woman's suggestive dance

parts.note: an innocent is a lamb, the stock image of guilelessness
Ada is a woman's name; the 's is 'has' or a possessive linking to the dance

explanation.surface: A naive woman performs a racy dance.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Brazilian partner dance famous for its sensual, hip-close moves.

clue.text: Cheese pub's displayed on occasion of special rivalry?

indicators.note: displayed on means placed above, in a down clue

parts.note: a local is one's neighbourhood pub; the 's is 'is'
Derby is an English cheese

explanation.surface: A cheese is on show in a pub on a special occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: A local derby is a match between neighbouring sports teams, often fiercely contested.
explanation.definitionFit: A game between two nearby rivals is a fixture charged with special neighbourhood rivalry.

clue.text: Change of heart for important city's elected head

indicators.note: change of heart means the central letter of the word for important is swapped

parts.note: major means important

explanation.surface: A city's leader changes their mind on something important.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle J of MAJOR is replaced by Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A mayor is the elected leader of a town or city council.

clue.text: Sort of island, say, viewed from the south

parts.note: Arran is an island off the west coast of Scotland

indicators.note: viewed from the south in a down clue means read upwards

parts.note: eg means for example, say

explanation.surface: A kind of island, for instance, seen from below.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort' is a verb here: to organise.
explanation.definitionFit: To sort things is to put them in order, organise them.

clue.text: Desertion from a place of duty, say, at sea

parts.note: a post is where a sentry or worker is stationed

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of say are scrambled

explanation.surface: Deserting one's post, as it were, at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Apostasy is abandoning a faith or cause, a form of desertion.

clue.text: Hue and cry loosely associated with Iraq's landowners

indicators.note: loosely means the letters are only loosely held together, so rearranged

parts.note: here the S of the possessive is kept as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: Public outcry is vaguely connected with Iraqi landowners.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of Iraq's counts: HUE, CRY and IRAQS together make eleven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The squirearchy is the class of country gentry who owned the land, collectively.

clue.text: Traitor seen regularly in port

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word Traitor

explanation.surface: A traitor is spotted from time to time in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the second, fourth and sixth letters of 'Traitor'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian seaport, often shortened in crosswords.

clue.text: Book is about Old English serving no practical purpose

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a book of the Bible

indicators.note: about means the word is goes round the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A book on Old English is of no practical use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old English' looks like one unit (OE) but splits: O goes inside IS, with E added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Otiose describes something futile or superfluous, having no useful function.

clue.text: Drink overcoming popular musician

indicators.note: overcoming suggests one word surrounding and so holding the other within it

parts.note: claret is a red Bordeaux wine
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: Wine gets the better of a popular performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarinet is an instrument, and by metonymy its player in an orchestra.

clue.text: OK after celebration? In the main a fearful sight

definitions.text: In the main a fearful sight

indicators.note: after means the second piece follows the first

parts.note: a jolly is a party or celebration
roger is radio talk for OK, message received

explanation.surface: Things are fine after the party, but out at sea there's a frightening spectacle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the sea; the pirate flag was a dreaded sight there.
explanation.definitionFit: The skull-and-crossbones pirate flag terrified sailors on the high seas.

clue.text: Here he solved a puzzle completely

indicators.note: puzzle is used as a verb meaning to muddle, so the preceding words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone here cracked a crossword in its entirety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solved' is part of the fodder, not the indicator; 'puzzle' does the scrambling.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being totally in love means utterly, so it stands for completely.

clue.text: Cruel beast so appearing as best?

parts.note: the word beast with its middle letter removed becomes best

explanation.surface: A cruel creature appears as the finest.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the heart (middle letter A) of 'beast' and you get 'best'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking compassion or pity, someone is cruel and unfeeling.

clue.text: Parents enforcing discipline perhaps giving big kisses

definitions.meaning: people who slap children as punishment

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both people who smack and noisy kisses, from the sound of a smack.

clue.text: City sign with line "Road Works here"

parts.note: Mobile is a city in Alabama
Libra is a sign of the zodiac
RY is an abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A town notice announcing roadworks in the area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Road Works' is not roadworks: it means literary works out on the road, in a travelling van of books.
explanation.definitionFit: A van lending books travels the roads, so written works are found there.

clue.text: Easily broken as litter bin's lid might be

indicators.note: lid means the top, first letter of bin
might be means the letters of litter could be rearranged

explanation.surface: A litter bin's lid could easily be smashed.
explanation.walkthrough: B (the lid of 'bin') is followed by RITTLE, the rearranged letters of 'litter'.
explanation.definitionFit: Brittle describes something hard but fragile, apt to snap or shatter.

clue.text: Go for second person? I agree!

definitions.meaning: it is your turn, addressed to you, the second person
said to accept a bet or challenge

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase both announces someone's turn and accepts a wager or challenge.

clue.text: Musicians from southern area abandoning the north

indicators.note: abandoning means the letter for north is dropped

parts.note: extent means area or size
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Musicians from the south leave the north.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of six performers is a sextet.

clue.text: Gallantry of companion bearing off first place in competition

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

indicators.note: off first place means the opening letter of the word for competition is dropped

parts.note: rivalry means competition

explanation.surface: A companion's gallant behaviour carries off top spot in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Chivalry is courtly, courteous behaviour, especially by men toward women: gallantry.

clue.text: Superior rating? Lowest? Not half!

parts.note: AB is able seaman, a naval rating

indicators.note: not half means half of the word for lowest is lost

parts.note: bottom means lowest

explanation.surface: A quiz on the rank of a superior: is it lowest? Certainly!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' looks like British slang for 'definitely' but halves BOTTOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Superior is the title of the head of a religious house, and an abbot heads a monastery.

clue.text: A song about heading for the Orient

indicators.note: about means the A-plus-song string is wrapped round the extra letter

parts.note: a tune is a song or melody

indicators.note: heading for means the first letter of the word the

explanation.surface: A song about travelling toward the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Orient' looks like the East, but 'Orient' alone is a verb, the definition; 'the' just supplies T.
explanation.definitionFit: To orient something is to adjust or tune it to circumstances, a synonym in that sense.

clue.text: Row after fine match is over

indicators.note: after means the letter for fine comes later
is over in a down clue means read upwards

parts.note: fit means match, as in clothes that fit
F is an abbreviation for fine, on pencils

explanation.surface: A dispute after a good match has ended.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor quarrel or spat is called a row in British English.

clue.text: Scoff when strike doesn't begin

indicators.note: doesn't begin means the word for strike loses its first letter

parts.note: beat means strike or hit

explanation.surface: Mockery when a walkout fails to start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoff' looks like mockery but is British slang for eating greedily; 'strike' suggests industrial action but is just hit.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to scoff food is to wolf it down.

clue.text: Sort of blue, meeting for seduction

indicators.note: sort of means a version or arrangement of, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A kind of blue movie meeting leads to a seduction.
explanation.definitionFit: Beguilement is charming or enticing someone, which is close to luring them into seduction.

clue.text: What to wear in second season, when it's less hot?

indicators.note: less means take away the letter for hot

parts.note: to season timber is to weather it
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Advice on clothing for the next season, when it is cooler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'season' looks like a time of year but is a verb, to weather (wood).
explanation.definitionFit: A knitted jumper is a garment, something one puts on to keep warm.

clue.text: Search bag for fabric

parts.note: to fish is to search, as in fishing for compliments
to net is to bag or catch

explanation.surface: Looking through a bag for a piece of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an open-mesh textile, familiar from stockings and tights.
